debts.title: Debts & loans
debts.subtitle: What you owe and what is owed to you, loans included
debts.dueDateHint: Optional. When set, the planner charges it on that day.
debts.withInterestHint: A bank loan, a car loan, a credit line — anything where the balance grows.
debts.interestFreeHint: Payments at the start that carry no interest. The rate applies to what is left afterwards.
debts.rateTypeHint: A floating rate is an index — Euribor, or the ECB's — plus the bank's margin, re-read every few months. Most mortgages are one.
debts.rateWatchInterestMore: {{amount}} more in interest before it is paid off
debts.rateWatchInterestLess: {{amount}} less in interest before it is paid off
debts.rateWatchPrompt: Pick a move and see what the payment becomes.
debts.fieldAmountBody: What the bank handed over — the capital. {{amount}} in the example below.
debts.fieldIndexBody: The market rate the loan follows, Euribor or the ECB's. You type today's value and correct it at each reset. {{value}}% here.
debts.fieldMarginBody: The fixed slice the bank adds on top. Typed once, and it does not change until the loan is paid off. {{value}}% here.
debts.fieldTermBody: How many monthly payments it is repaid in. {{months}} months, which is {{years}} years.
debts.fieldFreeBody: How many of the first payments carry no interest. Leave it at 0 if there are none.
debts.fieldRateBody: The rate you agreed, the same for the whole term. Only a fixed loan has one.
debts.rateHelpPartsBody: An index plus a margin. The index — Euribor, or the ECB's own rate — belongs to the market and moves. The margin belongs to the bank and stays the same until the loan is paid off.
debts.rateHelpWhenBody: Every one, three or six months, whichever the contract says. At each reset the bank reads the index again and works the loan out afresh.
debts.rateHelpEffectBody: The payment, not the end date. The bank works out a new payment on what is still owed, over the months that are left — so the loan still finishes on the day it always would.
debts.rateHelpExampleIntro: {{amount}} over {{months}} payments at {{base}}% index + {{margin}}% margin. Then the index goes up one point.
debts.rateHelpYours: Your loan, and what one point on the index would do to it.
debts.rateHelpPunch: One point on the rate is not one percent on the payment — here it is {{percent}} more.
debts.rateHelpAppBody: Every figure on a floating loan comes from the rate in force today. When the reset comes, update the index and the rest follows.
debts.loanCost: {{total}} in all, of which {{interest}} is interest
debts.payMorePrompt: Try an amount and see what it saves.

accounts.howItWorks: You type what each bank shows and what is in your wallet. The app compares it with everything written down since the last time, and the difference is what was spent or received without a record. Cash withdrawals and moves between your own accounts never need writing down. Money in Goals is taken to stay in these banks; money put into Investments is taken to have left them.

tour.settingsSubtitle: A quick look at what the app does

welcome.title: Welcome to MyFiWallet
welcome.body: All your money in one place: what comes in, what goes out, what is due and what you are saving. A look round in a minute.

quick.title: An expense in two taps
quick.body: The «+» at the bottom right is on every page. It learns your usual ones, like coffee or groceries, by itself.

transactions.title: Transactions & ledger
transactions.body: Every record, day by day. The ledger shows where the money went and where it came from, by category.

bills.title: Bills
bills.body: Electricity, water, rent, subscriptions. It reminds you before they are due, and you tap «Paid» when you pay.

incomes.title: Income
incomes.body: Salary, rent, benefits. Tap «Arrived» when they come in, and always know what you are still waiting for.

goals.title: Goals
goals.body: Put money aside for a trip or a home. See what is in, what is left and what it needs a month.

banks.title: Banks & cash
banks.body: Type the balance your bank shows and the app shows the difference from what you have recorded. Half a minute, when you are in a hurry.

planner.title: Planner
planner.body: What you will have by the end of the month, with what is due and what will come in. Ready — let's go!

demo.monthEnd: At the end of the month

stats.title: Statistics
stats.body: Where your money goes by category and by month, and how you are doing against before.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.body: The whole month at a glance: what is paid and what comes in each day. Tap a day to see what is on it.

investments.title: Investments
investments.body: ETFs, shares, crypto: what you put in, what it is worth now, and your gain or loss.

debts.title: Debts & loans
debts.body: What you owe and what you are owed: loans with interest, money from friends. Record each payment and see what is left.

demoMode.badgeTitle: You're viewing a demo with made-up data — nothing is saved
demoMode.noteBody: Create an account to keep your data. Changing your email and password, signing out and deleting the account come with a real account.

guidedTour.buttonTitle: Take a tour of the app

money.title: Money you have
money.body: What's in your banks and cash right now. Underneath, where that figure comes from.

payday.title: Do you make it to payday?
payday.body: What's left until the next pay, once bills and instalments are out. The chart follows your money day by day.

tiles.title: Everything at a glance
tiles.body: Bills, income, goals, debts: each tile sums up a page and takes you there in one tap.

quick.title: The «+» on every page
quick.body: Bottom right, on every page: on Goals, Banks, Investments and Debts it adds what the page is about; everywhere else a new transaction.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.body: Every record, day by day, with search and a category filter. Tap one to see or change it.

ledger.title: Where it went
ledger.body: The month by category. Tap a category to see the records behind it.

analytics.title: Analytics
analytics.body: Income, spending and savings over the months you choose; further down, your habits.

incomes.title: Did the pay come in?
incomes.body: Regular income waits here. When one lands, press “Arrived” and it's recorded for you.

bills.title: Bills still to pay
bills.body: One is already late, another is due this week. Tap a bill to pay it.

calendar.title: Calendar
calendar.body: The month day by day: when income comes in and when bills and instalments go out.

planner.title: Will I make it?
planner.body: With your own figures: what's left at the end of each month, as far ahead as you want to look.

goals.title: Goals
goals.body: The ring shows how close you are. Below it, what you've put in, what's left and the target as a whole.

accounts.title: Banks & cash
accounts.body: Now and then you note what each bank shows. Whatever you spent without recording it turns up here as “not recorded”.

investments.title: Investments
investments.body: Regular contributions or simple tracking, like this ETF: what you've put in and where it stands.

debts.title: Debts & loans
debts.body: What you owe and what you're owed, by bank or person: the car loan, the friend who owes you.

finish.title: That's it!
finish.body: All of this ran on made-up data that starts over on every refresh. Create an account to keep your own.

business.title: Business
business.subtitle: Your businesses, day by day: income, expenses, profit. The profit goes into your money.
business.emptyBody: At the end of the day, enter what each income line brought in and what each expense line paid. The profit goes into your money by itself.
business.legendTitle: How the figures are worked out
business.legendTurnover: “Turnover”: all the income of the month's closings; “Expenses”: all their expenses. They count only here.
business.legendProfit: «Profit» = Turnover − Expenses. Negative means a loss.
business.legendMoney: Each day's profit goes into your money as a “Business” income, on the card or cash you chose; a loss comes out of it as an expense. None of your categories changes.
business.ask_expenses: What did each expense line pay?
business.profitGoesInto: The profit, {{amount}}, goes into your money. Into which card, or cash?
business.lossComesFrom: The day closed at a loss of {{amount}}: it comes out of your money. From which card, or cash?
business.nothingMovesExplain: The day closed at zero: nothing goes into or out of your money.
business.noAccounts: No cards or cash on «Banks & cash» yet: it counts on the main account.
business.onlyProfitNote: Turnover and expenses count only on Business; only the profit (or the loss) reaches your money.
business.deleted: Closing deleted, together with its record in your money.
business.deleteClosing: The closing of {{day}} ({{name}}) will be deleted.
business.deleteClosingIncome: With it goes the income of {{amount}} from your money ({{place}}).
business.deleteClosingExpense: With it goes the expense of {{amount}} from your money ({{place}}).
business.ask_accountLoss: Where does the loss come out of?
business.calendarScope: Your closings, day by day. On each day: its profit (a loss with −). Above: what came into and went out of your money.
business.calendarKeySign: The figure on a day is its profit: turnover less expenses, over all its closings.
business.calendarKeyBoth: Both a profit and a loss on the same day — the total inside
business.overviewScope: The month, all businesses together: the closings added up.
business.ask_incomes: What did each income line bring in?
business.ask_businessDay: Which business, and which day are you closing?
business.emptyIsZero: Leave empty whatever had nothing today — it counts as 0.
business.amountBad: An amount isn't right: enter 0 or more.
business.noExpenseLinesHere: This business has no expense lines. A one-off cost goes in as an “other expense”.
business.oneOffNeeded: Each other expense needs a name and an amount above 0 — or remove it.
business.someAmountNeeded: Enter at least one amount, income or expense.
business.overviewScopeOne: The month of {{name}}: its closings added up.
business.firstBusinessBody: Give it a name, its income lines (e.g. Till) and its expense lines (e.g. Rent). Then each day closes in a minute.
business.bask_incomes: Where does its income come from?
business.bhint_name: As you call it — e.g. “Pharmacy”, “Street market”.
business.bhint_incomes: One line for each source of income; each day's closing asks an amount for each. At least one — a day can bring in 0 € too.
business.bhint_expenses: One line for each cost that comes back. You may have none; a one-off cost goes into the closing as an “other expense”.
business.bhint_review: Tap a row to change it.
business.incomeLineNeeded: Add at least one income line.
business.lineNamesClash: Two lines have the same name — rename or remove one.
business.lineGoesUsed_one: “{{name}}” goes; it is in {{count}} closing. Its amount stays as it is, under this name; it won't show in new closings.
business.lineGoesUsed_other: “{{name}}” goes; it is in {{count}} closings. Their amounts stay as they are, under this name; it won't show in new closings.
business.renameKeepsRecords: Records already in your money keep the old name (“{{name}}”); the closings show the new one.
business.businessReviewNote: Closings always show the current names — renaming changes no amount.
business.manageSubtitle: Each of your businesses with its income and expense lines. Make, change and delete them here.
business.goManage: Your businesses are made and changed in «My businesses»
business.daysOpen: See the month's days, one by one
business.lineSheetSub: Where the amount comes from: each closing of the month with this line.
business.closingSavedSub: It is in the business's days and already counts in the summary.

toasts.stillRunning: Still going — we'll tell you as soon as it's done
toasts.settingNotSaved: The change stayed on this device only — it wasn't saved to your account. Try again.
toasts.billDeleteFailed: The bill wasn't deleted. Check your connection and try again.
toasts.paymentUndoneWithExpense: Payment undone, together with its expense
toasts.repaymentSettled: Repayment of {{amount}} recorded — the debt with “{{who}}” is settled
toasts.categorySaveFailed: The category wasn't saved. Check your connection and try again.
toasts.categoryDeleteFailed: The category wasn't deleted. Check your connection and try again.
toasts.resetFailed: Your data wasn't deleted. Check your connection and try again.
